subject: SLA add-ons: bridge credit & rapid oncall ops — pricing and contract clarifications
messages:
From: Rachel Cole <rachel@bluepeak.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA addons: bridge credit for failover & oncall ops clarification

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime performance looked solid. We're pulling together procurement requirements and have two follow-ups before we can move to a term sheet:

1) Bridge credit: if we trigger a multi-region failover, can Redwood provide a prorated "bridge credit" that offsets incremental spend during the failover window? We're trying to avoid double-billing while we validate cross-region fallback.

2) Rapid oncall ops add-on: we'd like a documented response path (SLA tiers + escalation roster) for a 24/7 rapid response add-on. What does that cost as an add-on (monthly vs. committed retainer)? Any sample runbook or playbook would help.

We attached the SOW and a short appendix (BluePeak_SOW_Q2.pdf) that outlines our failover tolerance and expected traffic profile.

Can you send a short pricing sketch and whether any of this can be bundled for a discount if we commit 12 months?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Cole
Head of Cloud Ops, BluePeak Systems
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-02T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addons: bridge credit for failover & oncall ops clarification

Hi Rachel — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answers inline, and I've included attachment SLA_Packages_v2.pdf with the current pricing grid.

Bridge credit:
- We can offer a bridge credit that refunds the token spend delta for the duration of a platform-level failover event up to a 72-hour window.
- Example: if failover increases cross-region egress or reserved-node surcharge, we credit the incremental amount back as a percentage based on the SLA band (10% credit for Standard, 20% for Premium).

Rapid oncall ops add-on:
- Two purchase models: monthly add-on ($7,500/mo) or committed retainer (12-month retainer priced at $70k/year with included quarterly tabletop drills).
- Retainer nets additional triage hours and a named escalation engineer; monthly add-on provides business-hours triage + on-call callback within 60 minutes and escalation to onshore SREs during the next business window.

Bundling/discount:
- If you commit to a 12-month Dedicated commit (>= 4 GPU nodes) plus the retainer, we can provide a 10% concession on the Dedicated unit price for the first 6 months and waive the DocuSign setup fee.
- We'll document bridge-credit thresholds and the runbook in an addendum to the SOW.

Next steps: I can draft a short-term sheet with the concession and runbook appendix for your procurement team to review. If that works, I'll loop in Karthik to confirm margin/approval for the 10% concession.

Attachment: SLA_Packages_v2.pdf (pricing grid, runbook sample)

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA addons: bridge credit for failover & oncall ops clarification

Karthik / Laura — forwarding BluePeak's note. Quick ask: can we approve the concession below if BluePeak signs a 12-month Dedicated commit? I'm proposing: 10% off Dedicated unit price for first 6 months + waived DocuSign fee + inclusion of bridge-credit addendum.

Why I'm pushing: BluePeak is a fast-scaling enterprise account (BP-4279) — they're asking for documented runbook and a predictable failover credit to avoid buying redundant hot-standby across regions. They're ready to move quickly if we greenlight the concession.

Proposed counters to protect margin:
- Keep bridge-credit capped at 72 hours per outage and exclude configuration errors (customer-introduced).
- Require a minimum 12-month commit at >= 4 nodes or equivalent $T/month committed spend.
- If they request earlier termination, apply a 3-month termination fee at contracted unit rate less concession.

Quoted lines (for a short term-sheet draft):
- Dedicated concession: 10% off unit price (months 1–6)
- Rapid oncall retainer: $70k/year (12-month prepay) or $7,500/mo month-to-month
- Bridge credit: incremental spend credit applied per-event, up to 72 hours; credit rate tied to SLA band in SOW appendix.

Can you confirm margin OK or suggest where to tighten?
